prerequisites: Specific knowledge about manufacturing processes, materials science, graphic expression and industrial drawing.
Good knowledge of physics, mathematics and notions of automation and control.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Mechanical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Capacity for the prevention of occupational risks and protection of the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Interpret and/or prepare the necessary information for the correct development of a manufacturing process.
Plan manufacturing processes.
Develop Numerical Control programs based on the input documentation to the system.
Analyze the economic aspects associated with manufacturing in order to select the optimal conditions taking into account technological and socioeconomic aspects.
Apply advanced concepts related to product verification and inspection from the perspective of quality control.

syllabus_topics: Systems and information necessary for manufacturing
Parameters related to processes and economic aspects
Formulation of time and cost functions
Materialization of units and verification of shapes

assessment_methods.method: Practical laboratory knowledge (PL) through continuous in-person evaluation

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as (0.75 x E) + (0.25 x PL), where E evaluates theoretical-practical knowledge through a single written exam and PL evaluates practical laboratory knowledge through continuous in-person assessment. No minimum grade is required for E or PL. For differentiated evaluation, a single written exam covers both theoretical-practical content and laboratory practices, with the same weighting. If there are doubts about authorship or unauthorized means (e.g., AI tools), students may be asked for an in-person defense.
